solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Notices State features in TV programmes

indicators.note: a thing that features something has it within it, so one word holds the other

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state

explanation.surface: Public notices are shown as part of television programming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Features' is the containment signal here, not a noun for television items.
explanation.definitionFit: A series is a set of related television programmes broadcast in sequence.

clue.text: Too concerned with status, senior regularly visited club — ultimately mistake

indicators.note: regularly means at steady intervals, so every other letter of the word is kept

parts.note: first, third and fifth letters of senior

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: bish is British slang for a blunder

explanation.surface: An elderly person, overly status-conscious, made an error by visiting a club.
explanation.walkthrough: Bish is informal British for a mistake or botch.
explanation.definitionFit: A snobbish person sets too much store by social rank and looks down on those deemed inferior.

clue.text: Terribly irate about last-minute upset, hit back

indicators.note: in a down clue something upset is turned over, so the word is read from bottom to top
about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the other piece
terribly suggests something badly disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone furious at a late disruption strikes back.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged first word wraps round the second word written backwards; 'upset' is not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To retaliate is to respond to an attack with one of your own, to strike back.

clue.text: Award this writer upended? That's surprising!

indicators.note: upended means turned upside down, which in a down entry reads the word bottom to top

parts.note: my! is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A writer turned upside down over an award: what a surprise!
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's surprising!' looks like commentary but supplies an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: An Emmy is the American television industry's annual award, a statuette.

clue.text: Six longing to go back by a road leading to production area

indicators.note: going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the word is read right to left

explanation.surface: Six people longing to travel back along a road towards a factory site.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the longing goes back; the other pieces read in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A vineyard is where grapes are grown for wine production, so it is a production area in a loose sense.

clue.text: Knowledgeable, find more needing to be altered

indicators.note: something altered is changed in form, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A well-read person is advised to discover further facts, but those must be revised.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone informed has plenty of facts or understanding about a subject.

clue.text: Delightful at heart, Arsenal's supporters' sounds?

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its centre, so only its inner letters are kept

parts.note: letters from the core of Arsenal
football fans' noise from the terraces is chanting

explanation.surface: Fans at the football club's ground make a delightful noise.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club whose fans chant at matches; the setter takes EN from its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Enchanting means charming, casting a spell of pleasure over someone.

clue.text: Similar essentially calm President

indicators.note: essentially means in its essence or core, so the middle letters are kept

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of US President Eisenhower

explanation.surface: Two leaders compared: one is fundamentally an unflappable president.
explanation.definitionFit: Alike means resembling one another, the same in kind or appearance.

clue.text: City's animal sanctuary extremely cut off

indicators.note: cut off means a piece is chopped away, here the word's tail letter

parts.note: a den is a wild animal's lair or refuge

explanation.surface: A city wildlife reserve is badly isolated.
explanation.walkthrough: VERY loses its last letter to give VER.
explanation.definitionFit: Denver is the capital city of Colorado in the United States.

clue.text: Hall owner carrying permit

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the letters sit inside the neighbouring words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words, minus the first and last

explanation.surface: The owner of a hall has a licence on display.
explanation.definitionFit: To allow is to permit or let something happen; both are verbs of giving consent.

clue.text: Most desirable work — prison sentence reduced a little at first

indicators.note: reduced means made shorter, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work
doing time is serving a prison sentence

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of each following word

parts.note: first letters of a and little

explanation.surface: The ideal job, with a jail term cut a little at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimal means the best possible, the most favourable or desirable outcome.

clue.text: Way of speaking fine at first for daughter? Don't believe it!

definitions.note: the answer is a noun; the definition is a loose exclamatory gloss

indicators.note: at first for means in place of the opening letter, so one letter swaps in where another stood

parts.note: diction is one's manner of speaking
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A girl's elocution is said to be first rate, but the speaker doubts it.
explanation.walkthrough: The D at the start of DICTION is replaced by F.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiction is invented narrative, something made up and so not to be taken as true.

clue.text: Not good to involve learner, that's plain

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: L for learner, from the L-plate

explanation.surface: It is plainly wrong to involve a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: A bald statement is a plain one, blunt and without embellishment.

clue.text: Writing style from time in Paris, seen a lot initially, needs review

indicators.note: a review reworks material, so these letters are put in another order
initially means at the beginning, so the word's first letter is kept

explanation.surface: A writing style from a spell in Paris, much in evidence, requires critical reassessment.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalese is the clichéd prose style associated with newspapers.

clue.text: Given a rate has been changed, one's no beef or grouse?

definitions.note: a description of the answer: this person has no beef

indicators.note: changed means altered in form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: If a price has been altered, a customer has no complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: Beef and grouse both also mean a complaint, which is the surface; the setter means the meat and the game bird a vegetarian avoids.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegetarian eats no meat or game, so beef and grouse are off their plate.

clue.text: Sister, welcoming girl, one having winter fun?

indicators.note: welcoming means letting in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: SR is the abbreviation for sister

explanation.surface: A nun takes in a girl who is enjoying the winter.
explanation.definitionFit: A skater glides on ice, a classic cold-weather pastime.

clue.text: Dread having to include article — it's seen as light

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside the other

explanation.surface: Fear must include an article that is regarded as trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: Feathers are proverbially light, as in the phrase light as a feather.

clue.text: Right to be housed in redeveloped motel bringing calm

indicators.note: housed in means lodged inside, so one piece sits within the other
something redeveloped is rebuilt in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A legal right to stay in a renovated motel is soothing.
explanation.walkthrough: A lien is a legal claim on property, a less familiar meaning of right.
explanation.definitionFit: Emollient means soothing or softening, and figuratively calming a tense situation.

clue.text: Brief city delay coming up — song needed

indicators.note: brief means short, so the word is cut by its final letter
in a down entry coming up means rising, so the word reads bottom to top

explanation.surface: A short hold-up in a city calls for a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is a Renaissance part-song for several unaccompanied voices.

clue.text: Footballer's first-class finish? I'm not sure

parts.note: er is a hesitant noise of uncertainty

explanation.surface: A player's superb shot at goal, or perhaps not.
explanation.definitionFit: A defender is a footballer whose role is to stop the opponents scoring.

clue.text: African country lanes recalled, say, having been protected

indicators.note: something protected is enclosed, so one piece sits inside the other
recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone remembers the roads of an African state as being sheltered.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a country on the west coast of Africa.

clue.text: Unspecified person, girl, you briefly welcomed

indicators.note: welcomed means taken in, so one piece goes inside the other
briefly means in short form, so the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Some random girl gave you a quick welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' trims only the pronoun before it goes inside the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone is a pronoun for whatever person, no matter who.

clue.text: Clever bishop? Correct

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Is the bishop clever? Yes, quite right.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright is a synonym for intelligent or quick-witted.

clue.text: Like some gases refiner tries after cutbacks

indicators.note: cutbacks trim both ends of the phrase, leaving its core letters

explanation.surface: An oil refinery tests certain gases following budget reductions.
explanation.definitionFit: The noble gases are called inert because they barely react chemically.

clue.text: Those left feel not empty here?

definitions.text: Those left feel not empty here?

parts.note: a place's feel is its aura

indicators.note: empty means with the inside removed, so only the outer letters stay

explanation.surface: Diners who have gone feel well fed at this place.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes where people leave feeling full.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant is where you go to eat, and from which you leave no longer hungry.

clue.text: Force abolished as it's bad

indicators.note: bad suggests something gone wrong, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: letters to be rearranged with the next

explanation.surface: A force was disbanded because it was evil.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'as' after abolished is part of the letters to rearrange, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stasi was East Germany's secret police force, dissolved in 1990.

clue.text: Hint providing signal Labour leader must be accommodated

indicators.note: accommodated means given room inside, so one piece is put within the other

parts.note: a cue is a signal to act

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so the word's opening letter is kept

explanation.surface: A political hint that the party chief must be housed.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour is a major British political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A clue is a hint that helps solve a puzzle or mystery.

clue.text: Duo's expected standard, I admitted

indicators.note: admitted means let in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: par is the expected or normal level

explanation.surface: A double act has reached the usual level, one confesses.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair is two of something, the same as a duo.

clue.text: Annoying metal framework

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a grid of bars over an opening

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an irritating piece of ironwork, but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an adjective for something irritating and as a noun for a set of parallel metal bars.

clue.text: Back, bring up purpose of action

parts.note: to rear a child is to bring it up
an end is the aim or purpose of an action

explanation.surface: Supporting a plan: raising the aim of a course of action.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear end is the back part of something, as of a vehicle.

clue.text: Argument about Bible study figure

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: a tangle is a quarrel or fight
RI is Religious Instruction, a school subject

explanation.surface: A dispute about a key person in scripture classes.
explanation.walkthrough: RI, religious instruction, was the old British school name for religious education.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangle is a geometric figure with three straight sides.

clue.text: Plutocrat errs showing feature of moon

indicators.note: showing means putting on display, so the letters are visible inside the words

parts.note: the letters span the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A wealthy elite type makes mistakes about lunar landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: Craters are bowl-shaped hollows from impacts, typical of the Moon's surface.
